newsitem.title: BELGIUM: OECD sees Belgian GDP growth picking up.
newsitem.headline: OECD sees Belgian GDP growth picking up.

text.p: The Organisation for Economic Cooperation and Development (OECD) said on Thursday it expected Belgian Gross Domestic Product (GDP) to rise by 2.25 percent in 1997 and 2.50 percent in 1998, boosted by stronger exports.

Noting new fiscal measures aimed at ensuring that the general government deficit for 1997 would be less than three percent of GDP, the Paris-based group also said in its half-yearly report that the debt-to-GDP ratio was on a "firmly declining" trend.

"The decline in the debt-to-GDP ratio from 133.5 percent in 1995 to just under 125 percent in 1998 reflects, among other factors, the 370 billion franc debt reduction measures announced in the 1997 budget".

Returning to the prospects for the economy, the OECD said exports could contribute 1/2 a percentage point to GDP growth in 1997 and 1998, despite an acceleration in imports due to rising domestic demand.
Business fixed investment was likely to strengthen, reflecting good profits and a rising rate of capacity use.
Lower mortgage rates and a generally better economic environment should lead to a moderate pick-up in residential investment.
Conditions in the labour market would improve only slowly.
Private consumption inflation might decline to around 1-3/4 percent in both 1997 and 1998.
The main risks and uncertainties, on the external side, related to the future evolution of exchange rates and the strength of the upturn of continental Europe generally.
On the domestic side they concerned primarily the behaviour of households and whether -- and in which direction -- they might change the savings ratio.
